failure_summary.description: Calls omitted explicit criteria or required saves, duplicated work, or added unsupported extra operations.
A follow-up constraint was not applied to cached results, or was incorrectly treated as already complete.
Missing flight and hotel dates blocked a restaurant search whose destination was already known.
Flight time bounds were formatted incorrectly, and hotel dates were calculated or inferred without support.

patch.reasoning: Most observed cache, save, location-mapping, and domain-readiness failures already contradict explicit skill rules, so repeating them would add little. These edits address two narrow gaps exposed by the batch: explicitly mapping a named restaurant cuisine to its tool field, and treating “by” as an upper flight-time bound.

edits.content: For an initial restaurant request, map each explicitly named cuisine to `cuisine=[...]` in the same `search_restaurants` call, preserving the user's wording; a city-only search does not satisfy a cuisine-specific request.

edits.target: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`, and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`, preserving the stated AM/PM value.
edits.content: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X,” “by X,” and “no later than X” use `["12:00 AM", X]`; “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`. Preserve the stated AM/PM value.
